evals.prompt: We're launching a new skincare collection in 6 weeks. We have no email list yet. What should our launch plan look like?
evals.expected_output: Should check for marketing-strategy.md first. Should run the SLC readiness gate before the phased mechanics. Should walk through the five-phase approach (Internal Preview, Waitlist/Early-Access Build, Press & Creator Preview, Pre-Order/Limited Release, Full Launch), explicitly noting that with no existing list, Phase 2 (building early-access signups via owned/rented channel teasers) needs real lead time before Phase 5. Should recommend influencer/press seeding under embargo with adequate lead time. Should NOT reference Product Hunt, SaaS betas, dashboard stickers, or in-app tours.
assertions: Checks for marketing-strategy.md
Runs the SLC readiness gate before the phases
Walks through the five-phase retail launch approach by name
Flags that a cold list needs Phase 2 lead time before Phase 5
Recommends influencer/press seeding with lead time
Does not mention Product Hunt, SaaS betas, or in-app/dashboard mechanics

evals.prompt: We want to get press and influencer coverage for our launch. Any tips? We've never done it before.
evals.expected_output: Should walk through the Influencer & Press Seeding section: build a genuinely relevant seeding list (not just follower count), send product under embargo with adequate lead time (2-4+ weeks), give a clear specific ask and go-live date, prepare launch-day assets, treat launch day as an all-day cross-channel event, and convert the traffic spike into owned relationships (email/SMS capture) before it decays. Should note this is retail's equivalent anchor moment to a software launch-platform push, not a description of Product Hunt.
assertions: Covers building a relevant (not just large) seeding list
Recommends embargo timing with real lead time
Recommends converting the traffic spike into owned-channel signups
Does not describe Product Hunt mechanics (upvotes, hunters, PH algorithm)

evals.prompt: We just did a small restock of an existing product. How should we announce it?
evals.expected_output: Should classify this using the Ongoing Launch Strategy prioritization matrix as a minor or medium release depending on how notable the restock is, not a major-release full campaign. Should recommend a product-page update, a mention in the regular send, and not full fanfare (multi-channel campaign, influencer seeding) for a routine restock. Should distinguish this from a major release (new collection/flagship product).
assertions: Uses the major/medium/minor release prioritization matrix
Classifies a routine restock as minor or medium, not major
Recommends proportionate effort (page update + regular send) rather than a full campaign
Distinguishes from a major collection launch

evals.prompt: Our launch flopped. We launched 3 weeks ago and sales were way below what we expected. What went wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose against the five-phase approach and readiness gate — likely culprits include skipping the waitlist/early-access build (Phase 2) so there was no primed audience, weak or absent influencer/press seeding, inventory/fulfillment issues, or a product that didn't pass the SLC gate. Should ask what data exists (list size at launch, channel mix, whether Phase 4's pre-order data was fed into stock/marketing decisions) before prescribing a fix rather than guessing.
assertions: Diagnoses using the five-phase approach as a framework
Considers whether an early-access list existed before full launch
Considers inventory/fulfillment and SLC-gate failures as possible causes
Asks for real data before prescribing a fix

evals.prompt: How do we leverage partnerships and borrowed audiences for our launch? We're a small brand with no existing following.
evals.expected_output: Should walk through the Borrowed Channels section of the ORB framework: influencer/creator seeding, press/media coverage, gift guide and listicle inclusion, and co-branded collaborations. Should emphasize converting borrowed attention into owned relationships (email/SMS, loyalty enrollment) rather than treating it as the whole strategy. Should reference influencer-marketing, public-relations, directory-submissions, and co-marketing as the deeper skills for each borrowed-channel tactic.
assertions: Covers influencer/creator seeding, press, gift guides, and co-branded collaborations
Emphasizes converting borrowed attention into owned-channel relationships
References influencer-marketing, public-relations, directory-submissions, or co-marketing

evals.prompt: We're opening our first physical store next quarter. Can you help plan the launch?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is a physical-location opening, not a product/collection launch, and redirect to the new-store-launch skill instead of running this skill's five-phase product approach. Should note the two skills combine if a new collection launches alongside the store opening.
assertions: Identifies this as a store opening, not a product launch
Redirects to new-store-launch
Notes the two skills can combine for a collection launched alongside a store opening
